ties_disclosure.reason: This block's one drawn tub layer (Nwell 21/0) carries two deliberately differently-biased well classes, and klt 0.6.0 cannot express the split for a stream with no marker layer to select on. Fourteen of the fifteen merged Nwell shapes hold an n-tap reaching VDD; the fifteenth -- (176.820, 7.755)-(279.820, 12.555) um, holding the charge-pump dump buffer's two W=48u pfets -- is deliberately body-tied to its own source node cp.PSRC, as design/pfd_cp.sch itself specifies and as the PDK's own device-aware LVS extraction independently confirms (that well, its tap and its Metal1/2/3 rail are all net $30 in the committed pfd_cp.lvsdb, the same net pfd_cp.netcheck.log names cp.PSRC). A single ties[] entry grades EVERY shape of the declared well_layer against its own one net, so declaring net VDD reports a false erc.missing_tie on that fifteenth well; the well-side class selectors klt erc provides for exactly this shape (ties[].well_requires / well_excludes, klayout-tools#2339) select whole drawn shapes by interaction with a marker layer, and this stream draws no layer that separates the two classes -- verified by testing every one of the twelve non-Nwell layers the GDS contains: seven (22/0, 30/0, 31/0, 32/0, 33/0, 34/0, 42/0) interact with all fifteen wells, three (35/0, 36/0, 38/0) interact with ten wells and the PSRC well is one of the ten, and the two label layers (34/10, 36/10) hold only zero-area text and interact with none. There is no caller-assertion counterpart on the well side (the tap side has ties[].tap_boxes, klayout-tools#2234), so the tap is nameable and this build still cannot grade it. Filed generically upstream; see PROOF-erc.md, 'Upstream friction'.
